changelog: Insert a narrow_rule Core Principle that binds clause- or phrase-introducing function words to the following noun phrase or clause, preventing cuts immediately after articles, demonstratives, or clause-initial auxiliaries/particles; severe when detachment leaves a stranded fragment, mild when punctuation/parenthetical follows.
findings: When two candidate cuts are otherwise comparable, the prompt sometimes prefers splitting a verb from its required object while keeping an earlier adjunct cut; this orders fragments badly and should prefer preserving verb+object.

The prompt treats clause- or phrase-initial function words (articles, demonstratives, clause‑initial auxiliaries/particles) as independent cut-points, causing left-side fragments that harm cohesion or trigger contradiction.

diagnosis.why: Inserting the narrow_rule forced the model to avoid cuts immediately after clause- or phrase-introducing function words, so many cuts were shifted later (binding the following NP/clause into the preceding piece). That shift slightly improved alignment for moderate-depth budgets (bins ≤5–≤7) where multiple candidates are kept, but degraded the top-1 choice and the very short bin (≤3) because the strongest single cut was displaced or produced awkward fragmentation in quotes/NPs (illustrated by the worst examples where cuts moved off sentence-introductory markers onto nearby nouns/quotes).
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should keep the binding of function words to following material limited so it benefits mid-depth rankings (≤5–≤7) without displacing top‑rank cuts or hurting the very short-piece bin (≤3).
